title: Zyte Review (2026)
intro: Zyte is evaluated here as a web data / proxy collection platform — Zyte (formerly Scrapinghub) is a managed web-data collection platform — Zyte API for crawling/extraction rather than a raw residential-proxy GB pack as the primary shape. Pay-as-you-go plus monthly commitments from $100. $5 free trial credit. Same web-data-collection cluster as Bright Data. Bright Data remains the award (7.7); this entity does not outrank it. Distinct from IPRoyal’s $1.75/GB residential floor and from Apify’s Actor compute path. This review uses SoftwareGlimpse’s IT & Development methodology (ease of use, IT job fit, workflow depth, integrations, admin/security, scalability, value, AI), scoring products inside their job cluster rather than against unrelated peers. It is based on first-party research, not hands-on lab testing.
summary: Choose Zyte when a managed scraping API with a $100 monthly commit is the job — not Bright Data enterprise proxy commits by default.
verdict: Choose Zyte when a managed scraping API with a $100 monthly commit is the job — not Bright Data enterprise proxy commits by default. Compare Bright Data or Oxylabs for enterprise proxy estates; ScraperAPI for API-credit scraping; Apify for Actor compute; IPRoyal for cheap residential GB. Scores reflect first-party documentation as of 2026-08-18 — not hands-on product testing. Confirm current packaging, host/GB rates and minimums on the vendor site before purchase.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Zyte API is easier than assembling proxy + parser stacks; Scrapinghub rebrand is the naming tax. Not a lab test.
Web-data-collection — managed scraping API peer of Bright Data/ScraperAPI, not hosting or observability.
Crawl/extract API plus Scrapy heritage is deep for collection; less proxy-network catalogue than Bright Data.
Paid commits add governance; thinner public ISO-first packaging than Oxylabs / Bright Data.
Commits above $100 scale; enterprise SLA story is thinner than Bright Data.
Published $100 commit plus $5 trial credit is clearer than Bright Data ~$499; still not a $2/GB hobby pack. Affiliate economics excluded.
Extraction assist exists — scored as limited assistance, not a copilot suite.
